'''Eric Alexander Gaucher''' (born January 1972) is an American biologist best known for his work in computational [[molecular evolution]].

==Early life and education==
Gaucher was guided in biochemistry by Peter Tipton and Bayesian Theory by George Smith. Gaucher subsequently earned his Ph.D. from the [[University of Florida]] under the tutelage of [[Steven A. Benner|Steve Benner]] and Michael Miyamoto.<ref name=CV>[http://www.gauchergroup.biology.gatech.edu/docs/Gaucher%20CV_summer%202014%20copy.pdf Georgia Institute of Technology: Gaucher Group: Eric A. Gaucher: Curriculum vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161130200443/http://www.gauchergroup.biology.gatech.edu/docs/Gaucher%20CV_summer%202014%20copy.pdf |date=2016-11-30 }} (accessed 8 February 2016)</ref> Gaucher received the Walter M. Fitch Award from the [[Society for Molecular Biology and Evolution]] for his graduate work.<ref>[https://www.smbe.org/smbe/AWARDS/TheWalterMFitchAward.aspx Society of Molecular Biology & Evolution: The Walter M. Fitch Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812012718/https://www.smbe.org/smbe/AWARDS/TheWalterMFitchAward.aspx |date=2020-08-12 }} (accessed 8 February 2016)</ref> He then did postdoctoral work with [[NASA Astrobiology Institute|NASA's Astrobiology Institute]] in conjunction with a National Research Council Fellowship. After the two-year fellowship, Gaucher served as President of the Foundation for Applied Molecular Evolution.

==Career==
Gaucher was hired as an Associate Professor by the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] in 2008 <ref name= CV/><ref>[http://www.gauchergroup.biology.gatech.edu/people.html Georgia Institute of Technology: Gaucher Group: People] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151221233724/http://www.gauchergroup.biology.gatech.edu/people.html |date=2015-12-21 }} (accessed 8 February 2016)</ref><ref>[https://www.biology.gatech.edu/people/eric-gaucher Georgia Institute of Technology: Profile: Eric Gaucher] (accessed 8 February 2016)</ref> before moving to [[Georgia State University]] where he is currently a professor.  The Gaucher group conducts basic and applied research at the interface of [[molecular evolution]] and biology. As of February 2016, his [[h-index|''h''-index]], as calculated by [[Google Scholar]], is 25.<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=IrX5ZzQAAAAJ Google Scholar: Eric Gaucher] (accessed 8 February 2016)</ref>

Gaucher is also the founder and president of the early-stage biotechnology company General Genomics. His company exploits novel platforms to engineer proteins for the biomedical and industrial sectors.
